strongest_confirmed_findings: SEC-furnished slide 7: recent Q3 3-6 month contracts near $40M of annualized revenue per MW of power required to service related clusters; power boundary and margin undisclosed.
Approximately 70% of Q2 signed deals included customer prepayment; July pricing increased about 25% across SKUs. These are commercial/financing signals, not Q2 recognized revenue.
Final converts: $4.2B principal at 2.875% due 2033; $4.137B net before other expenses; $566.2M capped calls; derived $3.5708B before remaining expenses and $120.75M annual coupon.
10-Q: one undelivered 393MW site has rent capped at $14.7B/16 years and is excluded from the $35.5B uncommenced estimate; other uncertain leases cover 355MW.
investable_read_through: Short-dated ~$40M/MW-year pricing, July increases and older-GPU renewals challenge a blanket current neocloud glut thesis. The adjective is current/short-dated: 3-6 month duration creates rollover risk, and lease/debt intensity means strong bookings do not establish durable equity returns.
contradictions_to_prior_assumptions: Prior $9.54M-$13.39M effective-MW sensitivity used arbitrary PUE/utilization and all-cloud revenue; it is superseded without a numerical replacement.
The old 1.25GW Q2 midpoint is not selected: management says more than 300MW activated in June, and exact days/boundary remain absent.
$40M/MW-year is a signed-contract rate using power required for related clusters, not Q2 recognized revenue per IT MW, fleet yield, GPU-hour price or RPO conversion.
A 25% SKU price increase is not token-price deflation and cannot support an exact Jevons conclusion.
unresolved_questions: Compute-only recognized revenue, dated active AI IT-MW, active-power boundary, matched PUE and physical utilization remain missing; canonical revenue per effective MW and chips/MW are blank.
Identify cohort MW, architecture, customers, margin, prepayment, acceptance, termination and renewal terms behind the 3-6 month ~$40M/MW-year rate.
Map the 393MW and 355MW undelivered lease cohorts to customers, utilities, PPAs, SPV debt, guarantees and delivery remedies.
Quantify economic/replacement life by GPU generation; six years is only an accounting life for technology equipment.
